title: Long MU — Post-Q3 Beat Continuation (June 24 AH Earnings Binary)
entry: Enter $1,050–1,150 ONLY if Q3 FY2026 beats $35.5B revenue AND Q4 FY2027 guidance is above $36B revenue — both conditions must be met for entry. If MU gaps up above $1,150 on the initial AH print, do NOT chase; wait for next-session pullback to $1,100–1,150. If MU misses on revenue OR Q4 guidance is below $33B, do NOT enter — thesis is invalidated on the initial print. Scale: 60% on AH/pre-open confirmation, 40% on first trading-day close above $1,130. Avoid initiating if Samsung HBM4E qualification with NVDA is confirmed in the earnings call.
stop_loss: $990 daily close on a two-session basis — implies Q4 revenue guidance missed and Samsung's HBM4E is making genuine inroads into Micron's NVDA/Hyperscaler relationships; at $990, the thesis that HBM4 is sold out through 2026-27 is definitively broken; a single session close below $1,000 triggers a half-position cut; two consecutive closes below $990 trigger a full exit
targets: $1,250 — pre-flush recovery to May 26 area resistance; a Q3 beat-and-raise restores institutional confidence that the -11.4% KOSPI rout was non-fundamental and HBM4 demand is fully intact; +13.3% from $1,100 midpoint; take 40% of position
$1,350 — Q4 FY2027 guidance raised above $36B at analyst day in August 2026; HBM4 ASP holding above $25/GB confirms Micron's pricing power vs Samsung HBM4E alternative; +22.7%; take 40%

$1,450 — blue sky: Micron announces HBM4E qualification with NVDA ahead of Blackwell Ultra ramp (H2 2026); sell-side consensus PT upgrades to $1,500+; MU transitions from 'cyclical' to 'structural AI infrastructure' multiple; +31.8%; hold final 20%
catalyst: Micron Q3 FY2026 earnings tonight (June 24 after close, ~4 PM ET). Consensus after the June 23 KOSPI contagion flush: $35.75B revenue (some estimates revised to $34.66B post-flush), $20.83 EPS, 81.6% gross margin. Options market is pricing a 17% move in either direction. Key metric: Q4 revenue guidance above $36B would confirm HBM4 ramp is intact and Samsung HBM4E competition is manageable. The -11.4% drop on June 23 was driven entirely by KOSPI contagion (the KOSPI fell 9.99%, its largest single-day drop ever, triggered by MSCI Developed Markets exclusion flows from Samsung and SK Hynix) — not by anything Micron-specific. Pre-market on June 24 shows MU recovering +4.1% to ~$1,094–1,118, with the market already pricing a beat.
thesis:
The June 23 selloff in MU was the cleanest possible mis-pricing signal of the year: a -11.4% decline caused not by Micron's fundamentals, products, or competitive position, but by a mechanical KOSPI index de-weighting event in Seoul that had nothing to do with HBM4 demand, DRAM cycle positioning, or Micron's earnings. The KOSPI -9.99% was South Korea's largest single-day drop ever, driven by MSCI's announcement of a phased removal of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix from the MSCI Emerging Markets Developed Transition Index. Micron is a US-listed company with no KOSPI exposure; the contagion was entirely narrative-driven, not fundamental.

Micron's actual business position entering Q3 earnings is arguably the strongest in the company's history. HBM4 — Micron's high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators — is sold out through 2026-27 at prices well above conventional DRAM. The company's recent multi-year supply agreement with Anthropic (announced June 23, with Micron named as primary HBM, DRAM, and SSD supplier for Claude AI training and inference) demonstrates the demand pipeline is broadening beyond NVDA. Consensus gross margins at 81.6% would be a record high for the company. The Q3 revenue consensus of $34.66B–$35.75B implies 279% YoY growth — context that the AI memory cycle is still in its early innings.

The counter-party is the Samsung bear argument: SK Hynix and Samsung are both qualifying HBM4E (the next-generation product) with NVDA; if Samsung qualifies before Micron's own HBM4E production ramp is ready, Micron loses the pole position that supported premium ASP and the sold-out thesis. This is the single legitimate invalidation condition and is why the stop is tight ($990) and the entry requires the Q4 guidance beat as confirmation — the guidance is management's real-time assessment of competitive dynamics, not the Q3 backward-looking print. If guidance is strong, the Samsung risk is manageable for 2026; if guidance is weak, the Samsung risk is confirmed.
bull_case: Q3 beats $36B revenue AND gross margins print at 83%+, triggering a guidance raise to $37-38B Q4. Management explicitly confirms HBM4 ASPs held above $25/GB and there was zero demand softness from hyperscalers. MU gaps up 10-15% AH to $1,200-1,250. The stock reclaims its pre-KOSPI-rout level within 3 sessions. NVDA Annual Meeting same day confirms Blackwell ramp is on schedule — the combined print sends the AI semis complex up 5-8% on June 25. MU to $1,350 within two weeks.
bear_case: Q3 beats consensus ($35.7B revenue) but Q4 guidance disappoints ($32-33B) because Samsung's HBM4E samples passed NVDA validation at the Blackwell Ultra qualification stage, creating demand uncertainty for Micron's HBM4 into H2. MU drops 15-20% AH to $930-950. Entry thesis is invalidated on the print — do not enter. If already in, the two-session $990 stop triggers within 2-3 days.
invalidation: $990 two-day close; OR Q4 guidance below $33B revenue; OR management explicitly confirms Samsung HBM4E has received a preliminary NVDA qualification for any production volume; OR NVDA Annual Meeting warns of AI capex slowdown that reduces HBM demand visibility; OR pre-entry: Q3 AH drop more than 8% on the initial print (thesis is broken before entry)
